root_cause.text: During NVMe controller reset, `nvme_alloc_admin_tag_set()` allocates a new admin queue without first releasing the existing `ctrl->admin_q`, causing the old queue to be orphaned and leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `blk_put_queue(ctrl->admin_q)` call before `blk_mq_alloc_queue()` with the comment: "If a previous admin queue exists (e.g., from before a reset), put it now before allocating a new one to avoid orphaning it." The commit message explicitly states that a previous admin queue may still exist and must be released properly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the previous admin queue reference before allocating a new one to prevent leaking the queue object during NVMe controller reset/reinitialization.
intent_record.what: Added a check and call to blk_put_queue() before reassigning ctrl->admin_q, with a comment explaining the need to release any previous admin queue to avoid orphaning it.
intent_record.how: Prevents a reference leak by decrementing the reference count of the existing admin queue (if any) before allocating a new one, ensuring proper cleanup during reset or reinitialization.
